meters.label: Younger Dryas climatic event
meters.note: Multiple independent high-resolution proxies (ice cores, speleothems). Reality of the event is not in serious dispute.

meters.label: Global distribution of flood narratives
meters.note: Motif appears across every major cultural region with structural parallels. Distribution itself is significant data.

meters.label: Post-YD monumental architecture (Göbekli Tepe)
meters.note: Radiocarbon places earliest Layer III phases immediately after climatic recovery. Stratigraphy and architecture are robust.

meters.label: Pillar-city textual ↔ archaeological match
meters.note: Alignment is coherent; exact one-to-one identification of legendary sites remains debated.

meters.label: Parallel non-human intelligence motifs
meters.note: Widespread and structurally similar. Explanatory power high; precise identification interpretive.

claims.claim: The Younger Dryas constitutes a major, abrupt climatic disruption tightly dated to ~12.9–11.6 ka.
claims.support: Greenland ice-core δ¹⁸O, Asian speleothem records, and multiple lake sequences show synchronous onset within decades and a clear termination window.
claims.counter: Trigger mechanism is still debated (meltwater pulse, volcanic, cosmic impact/airburst, or combination). Timing of the onset itself is high-confidence.
claims.questions: What was the dominant forcing? How globally uniform were the effects outside the North Atlantic–monsoon domain?
claims.refs: Rasmussen et al. GICC05; Cheng et al. speleothem syntheses; PNAS 2020 timing study.

claims.claim: Göbekli Tepe’s earliest monumental phase sits immediately after the Younger Dryas termination and represents residual rather than de-novo complexity.
claims.support: Radiocarbon from Enclosure D wall plaster and associated charcoal cluster in the mid-10th millennium cal BC. Architecture is sophisticated and appears without clear local monumental predecessors.
claims.counter: Only a small percentage of the site is excavated. Gradual local development of symbolic behaviour in the preceding Epipaleolithic is documented elsewhere in the region.
claims.questions: How much earlier occupation exists beneath the current enclosures? What knowledge transmission mechanisms are actually required?
claims.refs: Dietrich & Schmidt radiocarbon work; Tepe Telegrams dating summaries; Sweatman calendar interpretations (debated).
